note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
The law says, “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.”

This is the wrath Josiah heard when the book was read. Manasseh and Amon were so wicked that the very book of the law had been lost, until Hilkiah found it in the house of the Lord. The king was meant to read the law before all the people, and the wicked kings had not done it.

When Shaphan read it before him, Josiah rent his clothes and sent to inquire of the Lord, “for great is the wrath of the Lord that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not hearkened unto the words of this book, to do according unto all that which is written concerning us.” The curses were written concerning them, and they had come.

precepts.text: Hilkiah the high priest found the book of the law in the house of the Lord and gave it to Shaphan the scribe, who read it.
precepts.point: All the people stood to the covenant to perform the words written in the book.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
“And Hilkiah the high priest said unto Shaphan the scribe, I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord. And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.”

That found book is the book Josiah read to the nation. He gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem, the priests, the prophets and all the people, small and great, “and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant which was found in the house of the Lord.” Our forefathers had the Bible, and the king read it openly.

precepts.text: Josiah sent to inquire of the Lord because great was the wrath kindled against them, for the fathers had not hearkened to the words of this book.
precepts.point: All the people stood to the covenant to perform the words written in the book.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
Josiah sent, saying, “Go ye, enquire of the Lord for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that is found: for great is the wrath of the Lord that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not hearkened unto the words of this book.”

Having seen why the wrath was kindled, the king did what the fathers had not done. He stood by a pillar and made a covenant before the Lord “to walk after the Lord, and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all their heart and all their soul, to perform the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people stood to the covenant.”

precepts.text: The Lord answered that he would bring evil on the place because they forsook him and burnt incense to other gods, and his wrath would not be quenched.
precepts.point: All the people stood to the covenant to perform the words written in the book.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
The Lord answered, “Behold, I will bring evil upon this place, and upon the inhabitants thereof, even all the words of the book which the king of Judah hath read: Because they have forsaken me, and have burned incense unto other gods”, “therefore my wrath shall be kindled against this place, and shall not be quenched.”

That word stood behind the gathering. Knowing the evil written in the book was coming because they forsook him and burnt incense to other gods, Josiah read all the words of the book of the covenant in the ears of the people, and made the covenant to walk after the Lord and keep his commandments with all their heart and soul.

points: Josiah begins to reign at eight years old and reigns thirty-one years, doing that which is right in the sight of the Most High and walking in all the way of David, turning neither to the right nor the left.

note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

points: In his eighteenth year he sends Shaphan the scribe to Hilkiah the priest to gather the silver brought to the house of the Most High and deliver it to the workmen for repairs.

note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

points: The money is given to carpenters, builders, and masons and for timber and hewn stone, and no reckoning is made with them because they dealt faithfully.

note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

points: Hilkiah the high priest finds the book of the law in the house of the Most High and gives it to Shaphan, who reads it. Manasseh and Amon were so wicked the very book of the law had been lost.

note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

points: Shaphan reports to the king about the money and the workmen, then tells him Hilkiah delivered him a book, and reads it before the king.

note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

points: When the king hears the words of the book of the law he rends his clothes, for the king was meant to read the law before all the people, which the wicked kings had not done.

note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

points: Josiah commands Hilkiah and his servants to inquire of the Most High for him and the people, for great is the wrath kindled against them because their fathers did not hearken to this book.

note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

points: Hilkiah and the king's men go to Huldah the prophetess, who dwells in Jerusalem in the college; there were women among the people who were prophetesses, known by their works.

note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

points: Huldah returns the word of the Most High: He will bring evil upon this place and its inhabitants, all the words of the book, because they forsook Him and burned incense to other gods, and His wrath shall not be quenched.
Because Josiah was righteous, repaired the temple, found the book, and began to keep the commandments again, he found mercy; yet the word spoken against Israel for its sin would still come to pass.

note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

points: But to Josiah, because his heart was tender and he humbled himself and wept before the Most High, the word is that he shall be gathered to his fathers and to his grave in peace, and his eyes shall not see the evil to come.
